//: The one record of what Greenhouse actually runs. The website is pushed from this file
(toolchain/ghcompat.py push) and the console reads it out of a signed `compat` package,
so a result is written once, here, and both surfaces follow.
Keyed by Steam app id: the website keys titles by name and the corpus keys them by id and
exe, and the app id is the only identifier the two can agree on. `name` is the PUBLIC name
as Steam spells it, which is what the website's Title rows use -- note that the corpus
calls app 2215430 plain "Ghost of Tsushima" while Steam and the site say
"Ghost of Tsushima DIRECTOR'S CUT". The app id is what joins them.
Verified results only. Community reports live on the website and are never shipped to a
console. `status` and `console` are the website's own enums verbatim (CompatStatus,
ConsoleModel), so there is no mapping layer to drift.
status: PERFECT  plays as it does on a PC
PLAYABLE plays, with the caveats in the note
MENU     reaches menus, or a little further, but is not playable through
BOOT     starts and shows something, then stops
WONT_RUN does not run; with `wall`, will not ever
wall:   steamstub | themida | eac -- a protection we will not defeat. Absent means the
WONT_RUN is a bug we have not fixed, not a refusal.
A title that is NOT in this file has no result, and both surfaces render that as silence
rather than as a guess. `version` is the loader the result was seen on; ghcompat.py check
warns when one falls too far behind the current build, because a stale version is the
whole symptom this file exists to cure.
`id` links to corpus/titles/<id>.ghtitle.json where a config exists. Most titles have no
config -- nine do -- and the walls have none at all.
